steps.say: Pelviureteric junction blockage is divided into two common mechanisms. An intrinsic aperistaltic segment is disconnected and cannot propel urine onward. Extrinsic compression is applied by crossing lower pole vessels in many adults. An accessory renal artery or vein is seen pressing on the junction. These vessels are found in thirty to fifty percent of cases. CT angiography is mapped before any repair is planned.
steps.tx: **Crossing vessels** (accessory lower pole artery or vein) cause adult **PUJ obstruction** (junction blockage) from outside in **30% to 50%** (three to five in ten), while intrinsic **aperistaltic** (non contracting) segments fail to propel urine from inside. Map vessels with CT angiography before any repair, because an unseen crossing vessel dooms an endoscopic incision. Choose dismembered pyeloplasty when vessels cross, since it transposes the junction away.

steps.say: Intermittent junction blockage is called Dietl crisis by urologists. Severe flank pain is felt in episodes with nausea and vomiting. The renal pelvis is overdistended behind the kink and then drained. Walking or standing with a mobile kidney is recognised as the trigger. Nephroptosis is blamed as the underlying mobility. Pain is eased after a large void is passed.
steps.tx: **Dietl crisis** (intermittent pelvic colic) brings episodic severe flank pain with nausea and vomiting as the renal pelvis overdistends behind a kinked junction, then eases after a flood of urine. It strikes walking or standing patients with **nephroptosis** (mobile dropping kidney) whose junction kinks with posture. Suspect it when colic alternates with a palpable loin lump, because the lump is the distended pelvis.

steps.say: Hydronephrosis on ultrasound is treated only as a suggestion of blockage. A dilated pelvis is sometimes just a harmless extrarenal pelvis. Diuretic renography is ordered to settle the question firmly. Technetium MAG3 is injected and furosemide is used to wash it through. Clearance half time over twenty minutes is read and reported as obstruction. Under ten minutes is accepted as normal drainage.
steps.tx: **Diuretic renography** (lasix washout scan) with **99mTc-MAG3** (kidney tracer) confirms obstruction when the **T1/2 furosemide** (furosemide washout half time) clearance **exceeds 20 minutes** (over twenty minutes), reads **equivocal between 10 and 20 minutes** (ten to twenty), and is **normal under 10 minutes** (below ten). Order it for dilated systems with preserved function, because ultrasound alone cannot separate true blockage from a baggy extrarenal pelvis.

steps.say: Equivocal scans are sometimes given pressure proof by testing. The Whitaker test is performed to measure pressures directly. Fluid is perfused antegrade at ten mL per minute through a tube. Renal pelvic and bladder pressures are recorded together on one trace. A gradient above twenty two cm of water is diagnosed as obstruction. The test is reserved for selected unclear cases.
steps.tx: **Whitaker test** (perfusion pressure study) infuses fluid antegrade at **10 mL/min** (ten millilitres per minute) while recording renal pelvic and bladder pressures together. A differential above **22 cmH2O** (twenty two centimetres of water) proves obstruction when scans equivocate. Reserve it for dilated systems with preserved function and unclear renography, because nephrostomy access makes it invasive.

steps.say: Dismembered pyeloplasty is kept as the definitive repair. The Anderson Hynes technique is used to excise the narrow segment fully. The ureter is reattached to the lowest pelvis for dependent drainage. A funnel is created to keep the anastomosis wide. Success above ninety five percent is reported by open, laparoscopic, or robotic routes. Crossing vessels are transposed behind the repair and fixed.
steps.tx: **Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty** (dismembered excise and reconnect repair) remains the gold standard, excising the aperistaltic segment and reattaching ureter to the most dependent pelvis with success **exceeding 95%** (over ninety five in a hundred) via open, laparoscopic, or robotic routes. It handles crossing vessels by transposing the junction anterior to them. Stent the anastomosis and drain the pelvis, because watertight healing needs diversion.

steps.say: Endopyelotomy is offered for selected primary narrowings only. A full thickness incision is opened through the stenotic segment from inside. The cut is placed posterolateral to dodge anterior crossing vessels. Strictures under one point five cm are required for best results. Minimal hydronephrosis with good function is needed as well. The incision is splinted by a double J stent for weeks.
steps.tx: **Endopyelotomy** (internal incision repair) makes a full thickness **posterolateral incision** (back outer wall cut) through the stenotic segment, deliberately avoiding anterior crossing vessels. Reserve it for primary strictures **under 1.5 cm** (below one point five centimetres) with minimal hydronephrosis and preserved function. Splint the incision with a double J stent for weeks, because unsplinted cuts restenose.

steps.say: Non dismembered repairs are kept for narrow roles. Fenger plasty is used to lengthen the segment by transverse closure. Foley Y V plasty is advanced as a pelvic flap into the ureter. Both are suited to secondary strictures and high ureteral insertions. Crossing vessels must be absent before they are chosen. Short strictures without vessel conflict are picked for these flaps.
steps.tx: **Fenger plasty** (Heineke-Mikulicz lengthening) and **Foley Y-V pyeloplasty** (pelvic flap advance) are non dismembered repairs for secondary strictures or **high ureteral insertions** (ureter joining high on the pelvis) without crossing vessels. Fenger closes a longitudinal cut transversely, while Foley swings a V flap of pelvis into the ureter. Pick dismembered repair instead whenever vessels cross, because these flaps cannot transpose anatomy.

steps.say: Timing of repair is planned to protect renal function. A solitary functioning kidney under block is given prompt decompression. Falling split function below forty percent is treated as forcing action. Pain with documented obstruction is also accepted for repair. Silent well drained systems are watched with repeat scans.
steps.tx: **Prompt correction** (early decompression or pyeloplasty) is warranted for symptomatic obstruction, a **solitary functioning kidney** (only working kidney) under block, or **differential renal function** (split kidney share) deteriorating **below 40%** (under four tenths share) on serial renography. Decompress urgently with a stent or nephrostomy when infection or pain supervenes, because pressure plus infection destroys nephrons fast. Watch silent systems with preserved drainage by repeat scans.
